--- js-build
name: JS Build

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"
      - "*.*.*"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}

jobs:
  build-js:
    name: Build JS bundles
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      TURBO_CACHE_DIR: .turbo

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.0

      - name: Restore Bun cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-bun-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-bun-

      - name: Restore Turbo cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-js-build-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'turbo.json', 'package.json', 'packages/**/package.json', 'packages/**/tsconfig.json', 'packages/**/src/**', 'scripts/**', 'src/**', 'vite.config.ts') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-js-build-${{ github.ref_name }}-
            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-js-build-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Generate node registries
        run: bun run generate:node-registries

      - name: Build node packages
        run: bun run build:nodes

      - name: Build package JS
        run: bun run build:packages:turbo

      - name: Typecheck app
        run: bun run typecheck:app

      - name: Build frontend JS
        run: bunx vite build

      - name: Build backend JS
        run: bun run build:backend:js

      - name: Upload JS artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: xiranite-js-${{ github.ref_name }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          path: |
            dist/**
            build/wails/xiranite-backend.js

#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { copyFile, mkdir, readFile, rename, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"
import { join } from "node:path"

const values = readArgs(process.argv.slice(2))
const nodeId = values.get("node-id")
const manifestPath = values.get("manifest")
if (!nodeId || !manifestPath) throw new Error("--node-id and --manifest are required.")

const root = process.cwd()
const manifest = JSON.parse(await readFile(manifestPath, "utf8")) as {
  node: {
    id: string
    name: string
    backendFeatures?: string[]
    nativeProbe?: { module: string; exportName: string }
    releaseGate?: { script: string }
  }
  snapshotId: string
  runtime: { minimumBunVersion: string }
  dataContract: { currentVersion: number; minimumSupportedVersion: number; maximumSupportedVersion: number }
}
if (manifest.node.id !== nodeId) throw new Error(`Manifest node ${manifest.node.id} does not match requested node ${nodeId}.`)

const backendFeatures = manifest.node.backendFeatures ?? []
await prepareStagedWorkspace(root, nodeId, backendFeatures)
// The staged package.json intentionally removes unrelated workspaces. Its
// lockfile is therefore a deterministic build-local derivative of the frozen
// source lockfile and cannot itself be checked with --frozen-lockfile.
await run([process.execPath, "install", "--no-save"])
await run([process.execPath, "scripts/generate-node-registries.ts"], { XIRANITE_BUILD_ONLY_NODES: nodeId })
await run([process.execPath, "scripts/build-packages-lazy.ts", `--only-nodes=${nodeId}`, "--skip-cli"])
// Backend declarations resolve against workspace package dist outputs. Check
// them after the staged base-package build, never against stale root outputs.
await run([process.execPath, "x", "tsc", "--noEmit", "--pretty", "false", "-p", "packages/backend/tsconfig.json"])
// The lazy package build deliberately skips native wrappers in normal app
// development. A standalone backend bundles their JS entrypoints, so produce
// those small TypeScript outputs before invoking Bun's resolver.
await run([process.execPath, "run", "--cwd", "packages/native-loader", "build"])
await run([process.execPath, "run", "--cwd", "packages/czkawka-native", "build"])
if (backendFeatures.includes("reader")) {
  await run([process.execPath, "run", "--cwd", "packages/arcthumb-native", "build"])
}
await run([process.execPath, "x", "vite", "build"], {
  XIRANITE_BUILD_ONLY_NODES: nodeId,
  XIRANITE_NODE_APP_ID: nodeId,
  XIRANITE_NODE_APP_SNAPSHOT_ID: manifest.snapshotId,
  VITE_XIRANITE_NODE_APP_ID: nodeId,
  VITE_XIRANITE_NODE_APP_SNAPSHOT_ID: manifest.snapshotId,
})
await rename(join(root, "dist", "node-app.html"), join(root, "dist", "index.html"))
await copyFile(manifestPath, join(root, "dist", "node-app-manifest.json"))
await run([process.execPath, "scripts/build-backend-js.ts"])
await copyFile(join(root, "build", "wails", "xiranite-node-app-backend.js"), join(root, "build", "wails", "xiranite-backend.js"))
await run([process.execPath, "run", "build:native-assets"])
await run([process.execPath, "run", "wails:syso"])

const enableReader = manifest.node.backendFeatures?.includes("reader") === true ? "true" : "false"
await mkdir(join(root, "build", "node-app"), { recursive: true })
await run([
  "go",
  "build",
  "-mod=mod",
  "-tags",
  "production,devtools",
  "-ldflags",
  `-w -s -H windowsgui -X main.nodeAppID=${nodeId} -X main.nodeAppTitle=${manifest.node.name} -X main.nodeAppSnapshotID=${manifest.snapshotId} -X main.nodeAppMinimumBunVersion=${manifest.runtime.minimumBunVersion} -X main.nodeAppBuildBunVersion=${manifest.toolchain.bun} -X main.nodeAppDataContractVersion=${manifest.dataContract.currentVersion} -X main.nodeAppMinimumDataContractVersion=${manifest.dataContract.minimumSupportedVersion} -X main.nodeAppMaximumDataContractVersion=${manifest.dataContract.maximumSupportedVersion} -X main.nodeAppEnableReader=${enableReader}`,
  "-o",
  "build/node-app/node-app.exe",
  ".",
])
await run([
  process.execPath,
  "scripts/verify-node-app-staged.ts",
  "--node-id",
  nodeId,
  "--manifest",
  manifestPath,
])
if (manifest.node.releaseGate) {
  await run([
    process.execPath,
    manifest.node.releaseGate.script,
    "--node-id",
    nodeId,
    "--manifest",
    manifestPath,
  ], { XIRANITE_NATIVE_ASSET_ROOT: join(root, "build", "wails", "native-assets") })
}
await run([
  process.execPath,
  "scripts/smoke-node-app-exe.ts",
  "--exe",
  "build/node-app/node-app.exe",
  "--node-id",
  nodeId,
  "--snapshot-id",
  manifest.snapshotId,
])

console.log(`[node-app] Staged ${manifest.node.name} (${manifest.snapshotId})`)

async function prepareStagedWorkspace(root: string, nodeId: string, backendFeatures: readonly string[]): Promise<void> {
  const packagePath = join(root, "package.json")
  const packageJson = JSON.parse(await readFile(packagePath, "utf8")) as {
    workspaces?: string[]
    dependencies?: Record<string, string>
    devDependencies?: Record<string, string>
  }
  const requiresReader = backendFeatures.includes("reader")
  packageJson.workspaces = [
    ...(requiresReader ? ["packages/arcthumb-native"] : []),
    "packages/api",
    "packages/backend",
    "packages/cli-runtime",
    "packages/config",
    "packages/contract",
    "packages/czkawka-native",
    "packages/file-operations",
    "packages/logging",

OK. So no embedded bun exists anywhere. The plan:

**Design**

1. Add a build tag-based embedded bun runtime mechanism in Go, mirroring the existing `local_backend_embed_production.go` / `local_backend_embed_dev.go` pattern:
   - `bun_runtime_embed_production.go` with `//go:build production && !no_bun` — embeds `build/wails/bun/<platform>/bun[.exe]` via `//go:embed`.
   - `bun_runtime_embed_stub.go` with `//go:build !production || no_bun` — returns unavailable.
   
   Wait, careful: Go build tag expression. I want: production AND NOT no_bun → embed. And `!production || no_bun` → stub. Those are complementary. Good.

   Actually, there's a subtlety: `//go:embed` of a file that doesn't exist fails the build. So for the "no embedded bun" build, the file must not be referenced by the embedding source file — which is why the tag split works. But the directory `build/wails/bun/` must exist for the production-with-bun build. CI will place the downloaded bun binary there.

   Also embed of a single fixed filename is nicer: `build/wails/bun/bun-runtime` — but the binary differs per platform and the same source file compiles per platform. Using `//go:embed all:build/wails/bun` and then selecting the right file at runtime by GOOS/GOARCH works and keeps one file. But that would embed ALL platform binaries present in the dir. If CI puts only the target platform's binary there, only one is embedded. That's simplest and cross-platform-safe: embed the whole dir with a naming convention `bun-<goos>-<goarch>[.exe]`, and at runtime pick `runtime.GOOS/GOARCH`. If the exact match is missing, fall back to any single file in the dir? Keep it simple: exact name match required; else system bun.

   Hmm, but for macOS universal? No, just arch-specific. Fine.

2. Runtime resolution order in `resolveBunCommand()`:
   1. `XIRANITE_BUN_BIN` env override (existing).
   2. Embedded bun (extract to cache dir, chmod 0755) — when built with embedding.
   3. System `bun` on PATH (existing `lookPathWithWindowsExt`).
   
   And "源码也对相应自动适配": the `service.go:551` spot that does `exec.LookPath("bun")` directly must use `resolveBunCommand()` too. Also the embedded variant should be preferred so a package without system bun works.

   Also: extraction. Embedded bun binary must be extracted to disk to be executed (can't exec from memory). Use the same cache dir pattern as `extractEmbeddedLocalBackendBundleTo`: `os.UserCacheDir()/Xiranite/runtime/bun-<hash>/bun`. For Windows, the extracted exe path. Careful about re-extracting 90MB every start — hash-based cache dir avoids that (checks existence first, like backend bundle does).

   Wait — there's a risk: on Windows, if the file exists and is locked by a running bun process, os.WriteFile fails. The existing code checks existence first and returns early, so that's handled.

func resolveBunCommand() (string, error) {
	if bin := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("XIRANITE_BUN_BIN")); bin != "" {
		return bin, nil
	}
	return lookPathWithWindowsExt("bun")
}

func localBackendScriptCandidates() []string {
	name := "xiranite-backend.js"

	candidates := make([]string, 0, 4)
	if exe, err := os.Executable(); err == nil {
		candidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(exe), name))
	}
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		candidates = append(candidates,
			filepath.Join(cwd, "build", "wails", name),
			filepath.Join(cwd, "build", "backend", name),
		)
	}
	return candidates
}

func lookPathWithWindowsExt(name string) (string, error) {
	path, err := exec.LookPath(name)
	if err == nil || runtime.GOOS != "windows" || strings.HasSuffix(name, ".exe") {
		return path, err
	}
	return exec.LookPath(name + ".exe")
}

func logPipe(prefix string, reader io.Reader) {
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(reader)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
		if line != "" {
			log.Print(prefix + line)
		}
	}
}

        with:

            ${{ runner.os }}-bun-

          restore-keys: |

      - name: Build node packages

#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"

type BumpKind = "major" | "minor" | "patch"

interface ReleaseOptions {
  bump: BumpKind | string
  dryRun: boolean
  remote: string
  tagPrefix: string
}

const repoRoot = new URL("..", import.meta.url)
const packageJsonUrl = new URL("package.json", repoRoot)
const repoRootPath = fileURLToPath(repoRoot)
const gitCommand = resolveGitCommand()

const options = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))
const packageJson = JSON.parse(await readFile(packageJsonUrl, "utf8")) as { version?: string }
const currentVersion = parseVersion(packageJson.version ?? "")
const nextVersion = resolveNextVersion(options.bump, currentVersion)
if (compareVersion(nextVersion, currentVersion) <= 0) {
  fail(`Next version ${formatVersion(nextVersion)} must be greater than current version ${formatVersion(currentVersion)}.`)
}
const tagName = `${options.tagPrefix}${formatVersion(nextVersion)}`
const branch = git(["branch", "--show-current"]).trim()

if (!branch) {
  fail("Could not resolve the current git branch.")
}

ensureCleanWorktree()

console.log(`Releasing ${tagName} from ${branch}`)

if (!options.dryRun) {
  packageJson.version = formatVersion(nextVersion)
  await writeFile(packageJsonUrl, `${JSON.stringify(packageJson, null, 2)}\n`, "utf8")
}

run([process.execPath, "install"], { dryRun: options.dryRun })

ensureNoExistingTag(tagName)
run([gitCommand, "add", "package.json", "bun.lock"], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "commit", "-m", `chore(release): ${tagName}`], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "tag", "-a", tagName, "-m", tagName], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "push", options.remote, `HEAD:${branch}`], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "push", options.remote, tagName], { dryRun: options.dryRun })

console.log(`${options.dryRun ? "Dry run complete" : "Released"} ${tagName}`)

function parseArgs(args: string[]): ReleaseOptions {
  const options: ReleaseOptions = {
    bump: "patch",
    dryRun: false,
    remote: "origin",
    tagPrefix: "v",
  }

  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
    const arg = args[index]
    if (arg === "--dry-run") {
      options.dryRun = true
      continue
    }
    if (arg === "--remote") {
      options.remote = requireValue(args, index, arg)
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (arg === "--tag-prefix") {
      options.tagPrefix = requireValue(args, index, arg)
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (arg === "--help" || arg === "-h") {
      printHelp()
      process.exit(0)
    }
    if (arg.startsWith("--")) {
      fail(`Unknown option: ${arg}`)
    }
    options.bump = arg
  }

  return options
}

Hash contents → `cacheDirectory/bun-<hash8>/<fileName>`; if exists with same size, return; else write with 0o755.

Careful about concurrent hosts: use temp file + rename for atomicity. The backend extraction helper writes directly; but bun is a 60–90MB binary, and two node apps may launch simultaneously. Actually, files created by a quarantined app inherit the quarantine xattr ("quarantine propagation") in some cases (apps downloaded from internet get flagged; the translocation etc). Chrome-downloaded ZIPs get flagged. For files written by a quarantined binary, macOS does propagate com.apple.quarantine. This could break macOS embedded bun execution with "cannot be opened because the developer cannot be verified" — actually for CLI binaries, quarantined exec → Gatekeeper prompt / kill.

Mitigation: when extracting on darwin, strip the xattr by... we can't easily run `xattr -c` (that's a system binary — /usr/bin/xattr exists; could exec it). func findProjectRoot() string {
	starts := make([]string, 0, 2)
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		starts = append(starts, cwd)
	}
	if exe, err := os.Executable(); err == nil {
		starts = append(starts, filepath.Dir(exe))
	}

	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, start := range starts {
		dir, err := filepath.Abs(start)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		for {
			if seen[dir] {
				break
			}
			seen[dir] = true
			if fileExists(filepath.Join(dir, "desktop", "node-runner-cli.ts")) {
				return dir
			}
			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
			if parent == dir {
				break
			}
			dir = parent
		}
	}

	cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
	return cwd
}

func fileExists(path string) bool {
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	return err == nil && !info.IsDir()
}

	data, _ := json.Marshal(value)
	return string(data)

```go
func embeddedBunAssetName() string {
	name := fmt.Sprintf("bun-%s-%s", runtime.GOOS, runtime.GOARCH)
	if runtime.GOOS == "windows" { name += ".exe" }
	return name
}

// embeddedBunContents returns the packaged Bun binary for this platform, or nil.
func embeddedBunContents() []byte {
	files := embeddedBunRuntimeFS()
	if files == nil { return nil }
	contents, err := fs.ReadFile(files, embeddedBunDirectory+"/"+embeddedBunAssetName())
	if err != nil { return nil }
	return contents
}

func resolveBunCommand() (string, error) {
	if bin := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("XIRANITE_BUN_BIN")); bin != "" { return bin, nil }
	if command, err := embeddedBunCommand(); err == nil { return command, nil }
	command, err := lookPathWithWindowsExt("bun")
	if err == nil { recordBunRuntimeSource("system"); return command, nil }
	return "", bunRuntimeMissingError()
}
```

```go
func extractEmbeddedBunRuntimeTo(contents []byte, cacheDirectory, name string) (string, error) {
	hash := sha256.Sum256(contents)
	targetDir := filepath.Join(cacheDirectory, fmt.Sprintf("bun-%x", hash[:8]))
	target := filepath.Join(targetDir, name)
	if info, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil && !info.IsDir() && info.Size() == int64(len(contents)) {
		return target, nil
	}
	if err := os.MkdirAll(targetDir, 0o755); err != nil { return "", fmt.Errorf(...) }
	// Write to a sibling temp file and rename so two hosts that start at the
	// same time never exec a half-written runtime.
	temp, err := os.CreateTemp(targetDir, name+".partial-*")
	...
	if err := temp.Chmod(0o755)  // os.CreateTemp makes 0600
	write contents, close, remove quarantine xattr, rename
	return target, nil
}
```

```json
{
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env bun\n/**\n * Stage the official Bun runtime binary that a production host embeds.\n *\n * The Go host looks the runtime up as `build/wails/bun/bun-<GOOS>-<GOARCH>[.exe]`\n * (see bun_runtime.go), so this script is the single place that maps release\n * targets onto Bun's own asset naming.\n */\nimport { mkdir, rm, writeFile } from \"node:fs/promises\"\nimport { existsSync } from \"node:fs\"\nimport { join, resolve } from \"node:path\"\nimport { tmpdir } from \"node:os\"\n\ninterface Options {\n  os: string\n  arch: string\n  version: string\n  outDir: string\n  force: boolean\n}\n\nconst defaultVersion = \"1.3.0\"\n\nconst options = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))\nconst bunTarget = resolveBunTarget(options.os, options.arch)\nconst assetName = bunAssetName(options.os, options.arch)\nconst output = join(options.outDir, assetName)\n\nif (existsSync(output) && !options.force) {\n  console.log(`[bun-runtime] Reusing ${output}`)\n} else {\n  await stageBunRuntime(bunTarget, options.version, output)\n}\n\nawait verifyVersion(output, options.version, options.os, options.arch)\nconsole.log(`[bun-runtime] Staged Bun ${options.version} for ${options.os}/${options.arch} at ${output}`)\n\nasync function stageBunRuntime(target: string, version: string, destination: string): Promise<void> {\n  const archive = `bun-${target}.zip`\n  const url = `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v${version}/${archive}`\n  const workDir = join(tmpdir(), `xiranite-bun-runtime-${Date.now()}`)\n  await mkdir(workDir, { recursive: true })\n  try {\n    console.log(`[bun-runtime] Downloading ${url}`)\n    const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: \"follow\" })\n    if (!response.ok) {\n      throw new Error(`Bun runtime download failed: HTTP ${response.status} for ${url}`)\n    }\n    await writeFile(join(workDir, archive), new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()))\n    await extractArchive(join(workDir, archive), target, workDir)\n\n    const inner = join(workDir, `bun-${target}`, process.platform === \"win32\" ? \"bun.exe\" : \"bun\")\n    if (!existsSync(inner)) {\n      throw new Error(`Bun archive did not contain ${inner}`)\n    }\n    await mkdir(resolve(destination, \"..\"), { recursive: true })\n    await rm(destination, { force: true })\n    await Bun.write(destination, Bun.file(inner))\n    await rm(inner, { force: true })\n    process.chmodSync(destination, 0o755)\n  } finally {\n    await rm(workDir, { recursive: true, force: true })\n  }\n}\n\n// macOS and Windows ship bsdtar, which reads zip; Ubuntu runners carry unzip.\nasync function extractArchive(archivePath: string, target: string, destination: string): Promise<void> {\n  const command = process.platform === \"linux\"\n    ? [\"unzip\", \"-q\", \"-o\", archivePath, \"-d\", destination]\n    : [\"tar\", \"-xf\", archivePath, \"-C\", destination]\n  const proc = Bun.spawn(command, { stdout: \"inherit\", stderr: \"inherit\" })\n  const code = await proc.exited\n  if (code !== 0) {\n    throw new Error(`Failed to extract ${target} Bun runtime (exit ${code})`)\n  }\n}\n\nasync function verifyVersion(runtimePath: string, version: string, os: string, arch: string): Promise<void> {\n  if (os !== processToGoos(process.platform) || arch !== processToGoarch(process.arch)) {\n    return\n  }\n  const proc = Bun.spawn([runtimePath, \"--version\"], { stdout: \"pipe\", stderr: \"pipe\" })\n  const stdout = (await proc.exited === 0) ? (await new Response(proc.stdout).text()).trim() : \"\"\n  if (stdout !== version) {\n    throw new Error(`Staged Bun runtime reports ${stdout || \"no version\"}, expected ${version}`)\n  }\n}\n\nfunction parseArgs(args: string[]): Options {\n  const parsed: Options = {\n    os: processToGoos(process.platform),\n    arch: processToGoarch(process.arch),\n    version: defaultVersion,\n    outDir: \"build/wails/bun\",\n    force: false,\n  }\n  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {\n    const arg = args[index]\n    if (arg === \"--force\") {\n      parsed.force = true\n      continue\n    }\n    const value = args[index + 1]\n    if (!arg.startsWith(\"--\") || !value) {\n      throw new Error(`Unknown argument: ${arg}. Usage: --os <goos> --arch <goarch> --version <x.y.z> [--out <dir>] [--force]`)\n    }\n    index += 1\n    if (arg === \"--os\") parsed.os = value\n    else if (arg === \"--arch\") parsed.arch = value\n    else if (arg === \"--version\") parsed.version = value\n    else if (arg === \"--out\") parsed.outDir = value\n    else throw new Error(`Unknown option: ${arg}`)\n  }\n  return parsed\n}\n\nfunction resolveBunTarget(os: string, arch: string): string {\n  const platform = os === \"windows\" ? \"windows\" : os === \"darwin\" ? \"darwin\" : os === \"linux\" ? \"linux\" : \"\"\n  if (!platform) throw new Error(`Unsupported Bun runtime target OS: ${os}`)\n  const cpu = arch === \"amd64\" ? \"x64\" : arch === \"arm64\" ? \"aarch64\" : \"\"\n  if (!cpu) throw new Error(`Unsupported Bun runtime target architecture: ${arch}`)\n  return `${platform}-${cpu}`\n}\n\nfunction bunAssetName(os: string, arch: string): string {\n  const name = `bun-${os}-${arch}`\n  return os === \"windows\" ? `${name}.exe` : name\n}\n\nfunction processToGoos(platform: NodeJS.Platform): string {\n  return platform === \"win32\" ? \"windows\" : platform === \"darwin\" ? \"darwin\" : \"linux\"\n}\n\nfunction processToGoarch(arch: string): string {\n  return arch === \"x64\" ? \"amd64\" : arch === \"arm64\" ? \"arm64\" : arch\n}\n",
```

```yaml
            goos: windows
            goarch: amd64
            runtime: bun     # embedded

          - os: windows ... runtime: system, embedded: false
```

--- js-build
name: JS Build

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
  push:
    tags:
      - "v*.*.*"
      - "*.*.*"

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  build-js:
    name: Build JS bundles
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      TURBO_CACHE_DIR: .turbo

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.0

      - name: Restore Bun cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-bun-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-bun-

      - name: Restore Turbo cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-js-build-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'turbo.json', 'package.json', 'packages/**/package.json', 'packages/**/tsconfig.json', 'packages/**/src/**', 'scripts/**', 'src/**', 'vite.config.ts') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-js-build-${{ github.ref_name }}-
            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-js-build-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Generate node registries
        run: bun run generate:node-registries

      - name: Build node packages
        run: bun run build:nodes

      - name: Build package JS
        run: bun run build:packages:turbo

      - name: Typecheck app
        run: bun run typecheck:app

      - name: Build frontend JS
        run: bunx vite build

      - name: Build backend JS
        run: bun run build:backend:js

      - name: Upload JS artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: xiranite-js-${{ github.ref_name }}
          if-no-files-found: error
          path: |
            dist/**
            build/wails/xiranite-backend.js

await prepareStagedWorkspace(root, nodeId, backendFeatures)
// The staged package.json intentionally removes unrelated workspaces. Its

func resolveBunCommand() (string, error) {
	if bin := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("XIRANITE_BUN_BIN")); bin != "" {
		return bin, nil
	}
	return lookPathWithWindowsExt("bun")
}

func localBackendScriptCandidates() []string {
	name := "xiranite-backend.js"

	candidates := make([]string, 0, 4)
	if exe, err := os.Executable(); err == nil {
		candidates = append(candidates, filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(exe), name))
	}
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		candidates = append(candidates,
			filepath.Join(cwd, "build", "wails", name),
			filepath.Join(cwd, "build", "backend", name),
		)
	}
	return candidates
}

func lookPathWithWindowsExt(name string) (string, error) {
	path, err := exec.LookPath(name)
	if err == nil || runtime.GOOS != "windows" || strings.HasSuffix(name, ".exe") {
		return path, err
	}
	return exec.LookPath(name + ".exe")
}

func logPipe(prefix string, reader io.Reader) {
	scanner := bufio.NewScanner(reader)
	for scanner.Scan() {
		line := strings.TrimSpace(scanner.Text())
		if line != "" {
			log.Print(prefix + line)
		}
	}
}
=== ci.yml ===
name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
      - main

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      TURBO_CACHE_DIR: .turbo

    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          submodules: recursive

      - name: Setup Bun
        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
        with:
          bun-version: 1.3.0

      - name: Restore Bun cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: ~/.bun/install/cache
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-bun-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-bun-

      - name: Restore Turbo cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: .turbo
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'turbo.json', 'package.json', 'packages/**/package.json', 'packages/**/tsconfig.json', 'packages/**/src/**', 'scripts/**') }}
          restore-keys: |
            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-${{ github.job }}-${{ github.ref_name }}-
            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-${{ github.job }}-

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile

      - name: Generate node registries
        run: bun run generate:node-registries

      - name: Audit React Compiler boundaries
        run: bun run audit:react-compiler-boundaries

      - name: Lint
        run: bun run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: bun run typecheck:app

      - name: Build node packages
        run: bun run build:nodes

      - name: Build packages
        run: bun run build:packages:turbo

      - name: Audit node architecture
        run: bun run audit:node-architecture

func TestStartLocalBackendSkipsDevProxyWithoutExternalBackend(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("FRONTEND_DEVSERVER_URL", "http://127.0.0.1:5173")
	t.Setenv("XIRANITE_BACKEND_URL", "")

	backend, err := StartLocalBackend()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected dev proxy mode to skip local backend without error: %v", err)
	}
	if backend != nil {
		t.Fatalf("expected no local backend in dev proxy attach mode, got %#v", backend)
	}
}

func TestResolveLocalBackendCommandUsesNodeAppEntrypointForDirectNodeHost(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv("XIRANITE_BACKEND_BIN", "")
	t.Setenv("XIRANITE_BACKEND_JS", "")
	t.Setenv("XIRANITE_NODE_APP_ID", "neoview")
	originalMinimumBunVersion := nodeAppMinimumBunVersion
	nodeAppMinimumBunVersion = "1.3.0"
	t.Cleanup(func() { nodeAppMinimumBunVersion = originalMinimumBunVersion })

	command, args, cwd, err := resolveLocalBackendCommand()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("resolve direct node host backend: %v", err)
	}
	if command == "" || len(args) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("expected one Bun node application backend command, got command=%q args=%#v", command, args)
	}
	if embeddedNodeAppBackendBundle().available() {
		if filepath.Base(args[0]) != "xiranite-node-app-backend.js" {
			t.Fatalf("expected embedded node application backend entrypoint, got %q", args[0])
		}
		if cwd != "" {
			t.Fatalf("expected embedded node application backend to avoid a repository cwd, got %q", cwd)
		}
	} else {
		if !strings.HasSuffix(filepath.ToSlash(args[0]), "/packages/backend/src/nodeApp.ts") {
			t.Fatalf("expected node application backend entrypoint, got %q", args[0])
		}
		if cwd != findProjectRoot() {
			t.Fatalf("expected node application backend cwd %q, got %q", findProjectRoot(), cwd)
		}
	}
}

func TestExtractEmbeddedLocalBackendBundlePreservesRelativeRuntimeAssets(t *testing.T) {
	bundle := embeddedLocalBackendRuntimeBundle{
		files: fstest.MapFS{
			"build/wails/xiranite-backend.js":                &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte(`require("./backend-assets/sharp.node")`)},
			"build/wails/backend-assets/sharp.node":          &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte("native-sharp")},
			"build/wails/backend-assets/reader-runtime.wasm": &fstest.MapFile{Data: []byte("reader-runtime")},
		},
		entrypoint: "build/wails/xiranite-backend.js",
	}

	script, err := extractEmbeddedLocalBackendBundleTo(bundle, t.TempDir())
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("extract embedded backend bundle: %v", err)
	}
	contents, err := os.ReadFile(script)
	if err != nil || string(contents) != `require("./backend-assets/sharp.node")` {
		t.Fatalf("extracted backend script = %q, %v", contents, err)
	}
	for _, asset := range []string{"sharp.node", "reader-runtime.wasm"} {
		if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(filepath.Dir(script), "backend-assets", asset)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("relative runtime asset %q was not extracted: %v", asset, err)
		}

#!/usr/bin/env bun
import { readFile, writeFile } from "node:fs/promises"
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url"

type BumpKind = "major" | "minor" | "patch"

interface ReleaseOptions {
  bump: BumpKind | string
  dryRun: boolean
  remote: string
  tagPrefix: string
}

const repoRoot = new URL("..", import.meta.url)
const packageJsonUrl = new URL("package.json", repoRoot)
const repoRootPath = fileURLToPath(repoRoot)
const gitCommand = resolveGitCommand()

const options = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2))
const packageJson = JSON.parse(await readFile(packageJsonUrl, "utf8")) as { version?: string }
const currentVersion = parseVersion(packageJson.version ?? "")
const nextVersion = resolveNextVersion(options.bump, currentVersion)
if (compareVersion(nextVersion, currentVersion) <= 0) {
  fail(`Next version ${formatVersion(nextVersion)} must be greater than current version ${formatVersion(currentVersion)}.`)
}
const tagName = `${options.tagPrefix}${formatVersion(nextVersion)}`
const branch = git(["branch", "--show-current"]).trim()

if (!branch) {
  fail("Could not resolve the current git branch.")
}

ensureCleanWorktree()

console.log(`Releasing ${tagName} from ${branch}`)

if (!options.dryRun) {
  packageJson.version = formatVersion(nextVersion)
  await writeFile(packageJsonUrl, `${JSON.stringify(packageJson, null, 2)}\n`, "utf8")
}

run([process.execPath, "install"], { dryRun: options.dryRun })

ensureNoExistingTag(tagName)
run([gitCommand, "add", "package.json", "bun.lock"], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "commit", "-m", `chore(release): ${tagName}`], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "tag", "-a", tagName, "-m", tagName], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "push", options.remote, `HEAD:${branch}`], { dryRun: options.dryRun })
run([gitCommand, "push", options.remote, tagName], { dryRun: options.dryRun })

console.log(`${options.dryRun ? "Dry run complete" : "Released"} ${tagName}`)

function parseArgs(args: string[]): ReleaseOptions {
  const options: ReleaseOptions = {
    bump: "patch",
    dryRun: false,
    remote: "origin",
    tagPrefix: "v",
  }

  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
    const arg = args[index]
    if (arg === "--dry-run") {
      options.dryRun = true
      continue
    }
    if (arg === "--remote") {
      options.remote = requireValue(args, index, arg)
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (arg === "--tag-prefix") {
      options.tagPrefix = requireValue(args, index, arg)
      index += 1
      continue
    }
    if (arg === "--help" || arg === "-h") {
      printHelp()
      process.exit(0)
    }
    if (arg.startsWith("--")) {
      fail(`Unknown option: ${arg}`)
    }
    options.bump = arg
  }

  return options
}

func findProjectRoot() string {
	starts := make([]string, 0, 2)
	if cwd, err := os.Getwd(); err == nil {
		starts = append(starts, cwd)
	}
	if exe, err := os.Executable(); err == nil {
		starts = append(starts, filepath.Dir(exe))
	}

	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, start := range starts {
		dir, err := filepath.Abs(start)
		if err != nil {
			continue
		}
		for {
			if seen[dir] {
				break
			}
			seen[dir] = true
			if fileExists(filepath.Join(dir, "desktop", "node-runner-cli.ts")) {
				return dir
			}
			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
			if parent == dir {
				break
			}
			dir = parent
		}
	}

	cwd, _ := os.Getwd()
	return cwd
}

func fileExists(path string) bool {
	info, err := os.Stat(path)
	return err == nil && !info.IsDir()
}

bunAssetName(options.os, options.arch)\nconst output = join(options.outDir, assetName)\n\nif (existsSync(output) && !options.force) {\n  console.log(`[bun-runtime] Reusing ${output}`)\n} else {\n  await stageBunRuntime(bunTarget, options.version, output)\n}\n\nawait verifyVersion(output, options.version, options.os, options.arch)\nconsole.log(`[bun-runtime] Staged Bun ${options.version} for ${options.os}/${options.arch} at ${output}`)\n\nasync function stageBunRuntime(target: string, version: string, destination: string): Promise<void> {\n  const archive = `bun-${target}.zip`\n  const url = `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v${version}/${archive}`\n  const workDir = join(tmpdir(), `xiranite-bun-runtime-${Date.now()}`)\n  await mkdir(workDir, { recursive: true })\n  try {\n    console.log(`[bun-runtime] Downloading ${url}`)\n    const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: \"follow\" })\n    if (!response.ok) {\n      throw new Error(`Bun runtime download failed: HTTP ${response.status} for ${url}`)\n    }\n    await writeFile(join(workDir, archive), new Uint8Array(await response.arrayBuffer()))\n    await extractArchive(join(workDir, archive), target, workDir)\n\n    const inner = join(workDir, `bun-${target}`, process.platform === \"win32\" ? \"bun.exe\" : \"bun\")\n    if (!existsSync(inner)) {\n      throw new Error(`Bun archive did not contain [\"unzip\", \"-q\", \"-o\", archivePath, \"-d\", destination]\n    : [\"tar\", \"-xf\", archivePath, \"-C\", destination]\n  const proc = Bun.spawn(command, { stdout: \"inherit\", stderr: \"inherit\" })\n  const code = await proc.exited\n  if (code !== 0) {\n    throw new Error(`Failed to extract ${target} Bun runtime (exit ${code})`)\n  }\n}\n\nasync function verifyVersion(runtimePath: string, version: string, os: string, arch: string): Promise<void> {\n  if (os !== processToGoos(process.platform) || arch !== processToGoarch(process.arch)) {\n    return\n  }\n  const proc = Bun.spawn([runtimePath, \"--version\"], { stdout: \"pipe\", stderr: \"pipe\" })\n  const stdout = (await proc.exited === 0) ? - `bun_runtime.go` + 构建标签拆分（`bun_runtime_embed_production.go` / `bun_runtime_embed_stub.go`）：解析顺序 `XIRANITE_BUN_BIN` → 宿主内嵌 bun → 系统 PATH；内嵌 bun 按内容哈希解包到 `~cache/Xiranite/runtime/bun-<hash>/`，临时文件 + rename 避免半成品；macOS 额外清 `com.apple.quarantine`，否则首次 exec 会被 Gatekeeper 拦。
- `no_bun` 标签编译出的产物完全不引用嵌入目录，找不到 bun 时报「请安装 Bun 或设置 XIRANITE_BUN_BIN」。
- `scripts/fetch-bun-runtime.ts`（新脚本 `bun run fetch:bun-runtime`）：按 `--os/--arch/--version` 拉官方 release，落成 `build/wails/bun/bun-<goos>-<goarch>[.exe]`，本机目标会实跑 `--version` 校验，并清掉其它平台的残留资产（否则 Go 嵌整目录会把别的平台一起塞进二进制）。
- `.github/workflows/desktop-release.yml` 取代 `windows-release.yml`：矩阵 windows-x64 / macos-arm64 / linux-x64 × `embedded-bun`(默认) / `system-bun` = 6 个构建，产物名 `Xiranite-<tag>-<平台>-<变体>`（win 裸 exe、mac zip、linux tar.gz），`publish` job 统一挂到同一个 GitHub Release；tag push 才发布，`workflow_dispatch` 只出 artifact。
- 顺带必须的跨平台适配（否则 mac/linux 作业直接挂在构建阶段）：`build-native-assets.ts` 在本平台 prebuilt 库缺失时降级为 0 资产并告警（原来无条件 `readFile` 崩），并修正 findz 扩展名 `dll/dylib/so`；`build-wails-local.ts` 增加 `--no-bun`、按平台决定是否 `-H windowsgui`/`wails:syso`；`service.go` 的 `NodeRun` 改走统一解析；状态里新增 `bunSource` 并在诊断面板显示 Bun 版本与来源。

**新发现并修掉的**
- **Linux 依赖装错了包**：Wails v3 alpha98 无 `gtk3` 标签时走 GTK4 路线，`#cgo linux pkg-config` 要的是 `gtk4 webkitgtk-6.0 libsoup-3.0 gio-unix-2.0`（证据：`~/go/pkg/mod/.../pkg/application/linux_cgo.go:17`、`internal/assetserver/webview/webkit_linux.go:6`）。原来我写的 `libgtk-3-dev + libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` 会卡在 pkg-config；已换成 `libgtk-4-dev libwebkitgtk-6.0-dev libsoup-3.0-dev libglib2.0-dev`。顺带确认了 `CGO_ENABLED=0` 时 `pointer` 未定义只是没开 cgo 的假错（`linux_purego.go` 要求显式 `purego` 标签），本地构建走原生 runner 就没这问题。
- **打包路径错**：`zip` 那步先 `cd build/wails` 再写 `../release/…`，实际指向不存在的 `build/release`，本地 bash 复现直接 `zip I/O error`。改成 `zip -q -j -X "$PWD/release/…"`，复验成员名是裸 `Xiranite` 且保留 `-rwxr-xr-x`（tar 同样验过）。
- **我自己引入的回归**：`production` 标签现在要求嵌入资产存在，所以 `bun run wails:build` / `wails:build:incremental`（你日常 Windows 本地打包）会挂在 `no matching files found`。已让这两条先跑 `fetch:bun-runtime` 并带上 `-X main.embeddedBunVersion`；独立 node app 打包（`build-node-app-staged.ts`）则显式加 `no_bun`，保持它原本「运行期检查系统 Bun 版本」的契约，也不给每个 EXE 凭空加 120MB。

**本地实测过的**：darwin 三种标签组合（`production` 内嵌 / `production,no_bun` / `production,devtools` 内嵌，mac 内嵌产物 90MB）、windows 两变体交叉编译（内嵌 148MB）、`go test -tags production` 真解包并执行内嵌 bun、根包全量 `go test`、`typecheck:app`、`check:source-size`、gofmt/oxlint、工作流 YAML 解析、6 个矩阵组合的 tags/ldflags 组装、publish 的 `find | xargs gh release upload` 收集逻辑。

**跑通的结果**（快照 `/tmp/xir-release-verify`，已清理）
`bun install → registries → 包构建 → typecheck → vite build → 后端打包 → 原生资产 → 落 bun → go build 两变体 → 打包 → 内嵌运行计时验` 全绿：内嵌版 99MB（zip 37MB，成员位 `-rwxr-xr-x` 保住执行位）、系统 bun 版 43MB（zip 14MB），`go test -tags production -run EmbeddedBunRuntime` 在打包机上真的解包并执行了内嵌 bun。

**因此发现并修掉的（每个都有本地复现证据）**
1. `build:nodes` 在 macOS 必挂：`clipm` 的契约导出跑 `uv`，其 lock 钉了 `torch==2.4.0+cu121`，只有 linux/win 轮子。`run-turbo` 虽然按 `xiranite.build.toml` 排除了禁用节点，但 `neoview` 依赖 `@xiranite/node-clipm`，turbo 仍把它拉进图里。→ CI 改用 `scripts/build-packages-lazy.ts`（它压根不构建禁用节点，且默认严格，任何启用的节点失败就退出码非 0）。
2. `build:backend:js` 在 macOS 必挂：`shell-integration` 里 `import("registry-js")` 的字面动态导入，bun 打包期就要解析，而它的原生二进制只有 Windows 有 → `Could not resolve: ../../build/Release/registry.node`。→ 非 Windows 时给 bun 传 `--external registry-js`（Windows 仍内联，行为不变）。
3. 矩阵写错了：`include` 条目不与 `embedded` 交叉，实际会产出 2 个 `runs-on` 为空的作业 + 3 个丢了 `embedded` 的作业。→ 显式列出 6 个组合。
4. GitHub release 下载会静默僵死（本机这一小时就稳定复现：两次 180s 零字节）。→ `fetch:bun-runtime` 改成流式落盘 + 180s 超时 ×3 重试，并新增 `--from <本地 bun>` 直接落资产；这也顺手补上了离线/内网开发的路子。

**边界与仍不知道的**：linux 编译只能等 CI（本机无 Docker，wails 的 `purego` 分支自身已坏）；mac/linux 的原生资产靠 best-effort 的 `refresh:native-assets`；runner 上的 apt/gh 行为、真实 `gh release upload` 都没跑过。9 个提交都在本地，工作区只剩你原有的无关改动。

**新增改动**
- `build-native-assets.ts`：`--refresh --only=<id>` 在平台库还不存在时不再 ENOENT 崩，空库按增量起点处理 → CI 里每个绑定独立成败（一个编不出来不会把另外两个一起清零）。实测：arcthumb 单独失败时，czkawka + findz 照样入库，步骤摘要如实记录缺失项。
- 顺手证实了 mac 侧 **三个绑定都能构建**：`arcthumb` 在本机 `build:native` 2 分 05 秒通过，最终 `build/wails/native-assets` 里是 `czkawka@12.0.0-api5, findz@0.1.0-abi1, arcthumb@0.10.1-api2` —— 所以 macOS 发布不会是残废版。
- `bun_runtime.go`：内嵌运行副本按内容哈希落盘，等于每次升级在用户缓存里永久留下 60–120MB。加了 30 天过期清理（只动 `bun-*`，保留当前项；删不掉的视为他机在用直接跳过）。这个清理是**可自愈**的：万一删掉了老版本还要用的副本，那个宿主会从自己内嵌的资产里重新解包。单测覆盖了「当前项/近期项/非 bun 目录/散落文件都不能被删」。
- `.gitignore`：`native/prebuilt/*` 只放行 `win32-x64` 与 README —— 我测试时生成的 darwin 库差点以未跟踪文件的形式挂在你工作区里。

**3. 补上默认发布承诺的测试盲点**：`TestEmbeddedBunRuntimeIsUsedWithoutSystemBun` —— 把 PATH 清成空目录后，production 构建仍解析出内嵌运行时并标为 `embedded`。之前只测了「有系统 bun 时优先内嵌」，没测「压根没装 bun」。

**CI 首跑请照这几条验收（把条目号 + 日志回给我）**

platform: windows-x64\n            runs-on: windows-latest\n            goos: windows\n            goarch: amd64\n            windowed: true\n            archive: none\n            output: build/wails/Xiranite.exe\n          - platform: macos-arm64\n            runs-on: macos-latest\n            goos: darwin\n            goarch: arm64\n            windowed: false\n            archive: zip\n            output: build/wails/Xiranite\n          - platform: linux-x64\n            runs-on: ubuntu-24.04\n            goos: linux\n            goarch: amd64\n            windowed: false\n            archive: tar.gz\n            output: build/wails/Xiranite\n\n    steps:\n      - name: Setup Go\n        uses: actions/setup-go@v5\n        with:\n          go-version-file: go.mod\n          cache: true\n\n      - name: Setup Bun\n        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2\n        with:\n          bun-version: ${{ env.BUN_VERSION }}\n\n      - name: Restore Bun cache\n        uses: actions/cache@v4\n        with:\n          path: ~/.bun/install/cache\n          key: ${{ runner.os }}-bun-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock') }}\n          restore-keys: |\n            ${{ runner.os }}-bun-\n\n      - name: Restore Turbo cache\n        uses: actions/cache@v4\n        with:\n          path: .turbo\n          key: ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-desktop-${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ hashFiles('bun.lock', 'turbo.json', 'package.json', 'packages/**/package.json', 'packages/**/tsconfig.json', 'packages/**/src/**', 'scripts/**', 'src/**', 'vite.config.ts', 'go.mod', 'go.sum', '*.go', 'build/windows/**') }}\n          restore-keys: |\n            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-desktop-${{ matrix.platform }}-${{ github.ref_name }}-\n            ${{ runner.os }}-turbo-desktop-${{ matrix.platform }}-\n\n      - name: Install dependencies\n        run: bun install --frozen-lockfile\n\n      - name: Generate node registries\n        run: bun run generate:node-registries\n\n      - name: Build node packages\n        run: bun run build:nodes\n\n      - name: Build packages\n        run: bun run build:packages:turbo\n\n      - name: Typecheck app\n        run: bun run typecheck:app\n\n      - name: Build frontend\n        run: bunx vite build\n\n      - #### Thinking

A real bug found! `zip` with `../release/...` failed: "zip I/O error: No such file or directory". Why? Because `cd "$(dirname output)"` → `build/wails`, and `../release` → `build/release` — NOT the repo-root `release/`! My earlier arithmetic was wrong: output is `build/wails/Xiranite`, so dirname is `build/wails`, and `..` = `build`, so it writes to `build/release/` which doesn't exist → error.

In the workflow, `mkdir -p release` happens at the workspace root → the zip path `../release/...` from build/wails resolves to `build/release` ✗ BROKEN. Must fix.

Fix properly: use absolute paths — `zip -j "$PWD/release/${base}.zip" "${output}"`? `-j` junk paths so the member name is just `Xiranite` ✓ and no subshell needed. Clean:

```bash
zip -q -j -X "$PWD/release/${base}.zip" "${{ matrix.output }}"
```
Wait: `-j` "store just the name of the saved file (no directory)" ✓ — member becomes `Xiranite` ✓.

And tar: `tar -C "$(dirname output)" -czf "release/..." "$(basename output)"` — with `-C`, the `-f` path is resolved relative to... GNU/BSD tar resolves the archive path relative to the ORIGINAL cwd? `-C` affects subsequent file args, but the archive file is opened before the -C switch is applied? In GNU tar, options are processed in order; `-C dir` changes directory for *following* operands, and `-f` file is opened relative to the cwd at the time of opening (start), which is the original cwd → `release/...` ✓ works (that's how I wrote it: `-C dir -czf release/...` — hmm, the archive `-f` comes AFTER -C in my command: `tar -C dir -czf release/x.tar.gz name`. GNU tar parses all options first; -f is opened before chdir? Risky. Better to make the archive path absolute too.

Let me use absolute paths for both and verify with the rehearsal:
```bash
zip -q -j -X "$PWD/release/${base}.zip" "${{ matrix.output }}"
tar -C "$(dirname "${{ matrix.output }}")" -czf "$PWD/release/${base}.tar.gz" "$(basename "${{ matrix.output }}")"
```
Also check exec bit preservation: zip stores external attrs (mode) ✓ bsdtar/zip on macOS store unix modes; `unzip` on macOS restores them ✓. tar gz ✓ obviously.

# workflow_dispatch keeps the branch name in GITHUB_REF_NAME, which may

GitHub's rule: `include` entries whose keys don't conflict are added to *each* existing matrix combination? The documented behavior: "For each object in include, if the key doesn't exist in the matrix, a new object is added to the matrix" — CAREFUL! There are two cases:
- If an include object's keys **match** existing matrix keys (i.e., it adds a new value for an existing key like `os: [...]` + `include: [{os: A, extra}]`), it augments that combination.
- If the include object contains **no keys that exist in the matrix**, GitHub **adds each include object as a new separate job** (appended to the matrix, not crossed)!

Yes — that's the documented subtlety: "If you specify a matrix with include objects that don't share any key with the matrix, each include object is added as a new configuration" — i.e., you'd get 2 (from embedded) + 3 (from include) = 5 jobs?? Actually the canonical documented rule from GitHub:

> "If you use the include keyword with the matrix values of an existing matrix variable, it creates a new matrix variable... For example, matrix os: [macos, ubuntu, windows] with include entries that add `xcode: 12.2` for macos." 
> "Adding values that don't match any existing variable creates new jobs rather than cross product."

The precise wording from the docs: "For example, this workflow ... The include job that uses the same os key adds arch... **Any other object (with keys that don't exist in the matrix) is added as a new, single job configuration**."

set -euo pipefail
# workflow_dispatch keeps the branch name in GITHUB_REF_NAME, which may
# contain a slash and would break the asset path.
version="${GITHUB_REF_NAME//\//_}"
variant=$([ "${{ matrix.embedded }}" = "true" ] && echo "embedded-bun" || echo "system-bun")
base="Xiranite-${version}-${{ matrix.platform }}-${variant}"
mkdir -p release
case "${{ matrix.archive }}" in
  zip)
    # -j keeps the archived member name bare; $PWD anchors the
    # destination at the workspace root, which a relative ../release
    # resolved against the binary directory would miss.
    zip -q -j -X "$PWD/release/${base}.zip" "${{ matrix.output }}"
    ;;
  tar.gz)
    tar -C "$(dirname "${{ matrix.output }}")" -czf "$PWD/release/${base}.tar.gz" "$(basename "${{ matrix.output }}")"
    ;;
  *)
    cp "${{ matrix.output }}" "release/${base}.exe"
    ;;
esac

The fetch process (17608) is alive but its temp work dir is empty after ~10 min → the `fetch()` to github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download is hanging (no bytes written since we only writeFile after the full arrayBuffer). That's a real robustness problem in my script too: 

1. **No timeout** on the download → a flaky network hangs the CI job indefinitely (GH Actions has a 6h job timeout; that would waste the whole run).
2. Buffering the whole 60-120MB via `arrayBuffer()` is memory-heavy and hides progress.

Fix both: 
- Add an AbortSignal timeout (e.g. 120s) + a couple of retries with backoff.
- Stream the response body to disk instead of buffering: `Bun.write(dest, response.body)` supports streams ✓ (Bun.write accepts a Response or ReadableStream).

This matters for CI reliability (GitHub runners also hit transient GitHub release download failures — memory says GitHub reachability is flaky on the Windows box too).

```ts
const downloadTimeoutMs = 180_000
const downloadAttempts = 3

async function downloadArchive(url: string, destination: string): Promise<void> {
  let lastError: unknown
  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= downloadAttempts; attempt += 1) {
    // GitHub release downloads intermittently stall on both developer machines
    // and runners, so a hung fetch must fail into a retry instead of eating the
    // whole CI job timeout.
    const controller = new AbortController()
    const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(new Error(`download timed out`)), downloadTimeoutMs)
    try {
      const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: "follow", signal: controller.signal })
      if (!response.ok) throw new Error(`HTTP ${response.status} for ${url}`)
      if (!response.body) throw new Error(`empty response body for ${url}`)
      await writeFile(destination, response.body)   // does Bun.write accept a ReadableStream? Bun.write(dest, data) accepts Response | ReadableStream ✓
      return
    } catch (error) {
      lastError = error
      console.warn(`[bun-runtime] Attempt ${attempt}/${downloadAttempts} failed: ${(error as Error).message}`)
      await Bun.sleep(2_000 * attempt)
    } finally {
      clearTimeout(timer)
    }
  }
  throw new Error(`Bun runtime download failed after ${downloadAttempts} attempts: ${String(lastError)}`)
}
```
Careful: `writeFile` from node:fs/promises doesn't accept a stream. Use `Bun.write(destination, response.body)` (Bun supports ReadableStream/Response) ✓. Actually simplest: `await Bun.write(destination, response)` — Bun.write accepts a Response and streams the body ✓.

Since the file already uses `Bun.write(destination, Bun.file(inner))` elsewhere ✓ Bun.write is available.

Also keep the `writeFile` import only if still used — after this change, `writeFile` may become unused. Let me restructure stageBunRuntime to call downloadArchive into workDir.

84	async function stageBunRuntime(target: string, version: string, destination: string, targetOs: string): Promise<void> {
85	  const archive = `bun-${target}.zip`
86	  const url = `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v${version}/${archive}`
87	  const workDir = join(tmpdir(), `xiranite-bun-runtime-${Date.now()}`)
88	  await mkdir(workDir, { recursive: true })
89	  try {
90	    console.log(`[bun-runtime] Downloading ${url}`)
91	    await downloadArchive(url, join(workDir, archive))
92	    await extractArchive(join(workDir, archive), target, workDir)
93	
94	    // The archive member follows the target OS, not the machine running the build.
95	    const inner = join(workDir, `bun-${target}`, targetOs === "windows" ? "bun.exe" : "bun")
96	    if (!existsSync(inner)) {
97	      throw new Error(`Bun archive did not contain ${inner}`)
98	    }
99	    await mkdir(resolve(destination, ".."), { recursive: true })
100	    await rm(destination, { force: true })
101	    await Bun.write(destination, Bun.file(inner))
102	    await chmod(destination, 0o755)
103	  } finally {
104	    await rm(workDir, { recursive: true, force: true })
105	  }
106	}

108	// GitHub release downloads stall intermittently on both developer machines and
109	// runners, so the transfer is bounded and retried instead of leaving the whole
110	// build waiting on one connection until the CI job times out.
111	async function downloadArchive(url: string, destination: string): Promise<void> {
112	  const attempts = 3
113	  let lastError: unknown
114	  for (let attempt = 1; attempt <= attempts; attempt += 1) {
115	    const controller = new AbortController()
116	    const timeout = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(new Error(`no completion within ${downloadTimeoutMs / 1000}s`)), downloadTimeoutMs)
117	    try {
118	      const response = await fetch(url, { redirect: "follow", signal: controller.signal })
119	      if (!response.ok || !response.body) {
120	        throw new Error(`Bun runtime download failed: HTTP ${response.status} for ${url}`)
121	      }
122	      await Bun.write(destination, response)
123	      return
124	    } catch (error) {
125	      lastError = error
126	      console.warn(`[bun-runtime] Download attempt ${attempt}/${attempts} failed: ${(error as Error).message}`)
127	      await rm(destination, { force: true })
128	      if (attempt < attempts) await Bun.sleep(attempt * 5_000)
129	    } finally {
130	      clearTimeout(timeout)
131	    }
132	  }
133	  throw new Error(`Bun runtime download failed after ${attempts} attempts: ${String(lastError)}`)
134	}
135	
136	// macOS and Windows ship bsdtar, which reads zip; Ubuntu runners carry unzip.
137	async function extractArchive(archivePath: string, target: string, destination: string): Promise<void> {
138	  const command = process.platform === "linux"
139	    ? ["unzip", "-q", "-o", archivePath, "-d", destination]
140	    : ["tar", "-xf", archivePath, "-C", destination]
141	  const proc = Bun.spawn(command, { stdout: "inherit", stderr: "inherit" })
142	  const code = await proc.exited
143	  if (code !== 0) {
144	    throw new Error(`Failed to extract ${target} Bun runtime (exit ${code})`)
145	  }
146	}
147	
148	async function verifyVersion(runtimePath: string, version: string, os: string, arch: string): Promise<void> {
149	  if (os !== processToGoos(process.platform) || arch !== processToGoarch(process.arch)) {
150	    return
151	  }
152	  const proc = Bun.spawn([runtimePath, "--version"], { stdout: "pipe", stderr: "pipe" })
153	  const stdout = (await proc.exited === 0) ? (await new Response(proc.stdout).text()).trim() : ""
154	  if (stdout !== version) {
155	    throw new Error(`Staged Bun runtime reports ${stdout || "no version"}, expected ${version}`)
156	  }
157	}
158	
159	function parseArgs(args: string[]): Options {
160	  const parsed: Options = {
161	    os: processToGoos(process.platform),
162	    arch: processToGoarch(process.arch),
163	    outDir: "build/wails/bun",
164	    force: false,
165	  }
166	  for (let index = 0; index < args.length; index += 1) {
167	    const arg = args[index]
168	    if (arg === "--force") {
169	      parsed.force = true
170	      continue
171	    }
172	    const value = args[index + 1]
173	    if (!arg.startsWith("--") || !value) {
174	      throw new Error(`Unknown argument: ${arg}. Usage: --os <goos> --arch <goarch> --version <x.y.z> [--out <dir>] [--force]`)
175	    }
176	    index += 1
177	    if (arg === "--os") parsed.os = value
178	    else if (arg === "--arch") parsed.arch = value
179	    else if (arg === "--version") parsed.version = value
180	    else if (arg === "--out") parsed.outDir = value
181	    else throw new Error(`Unknown option: ${arg}`)
182	  }
183	  return parsed
184	}
185	
186	function resolveBunTarget(os: string, arch: string): string {
187	  const platform = os === "windows" ? "windows" : os === "darwin" ? "darwin" : os === "linux" ? "linux" : ""
188	  if (!platform) throw new Error(`Unsupported Bun runtime target OS: ${os}`)
189	  const cpu = arch === "amd64" ? "x64" : arch === "arm64" ? "aarch64" : ""
190	  if (!cpu) throw new Error(`Unsupported Bun runtime target architecture: ${arch}`)
191	  return `${platform}-${cpu}`
192	}
193	
194	function bunAssetName(os: string, arch: string): string {
195	  const name = `bun-${os}-${arch}`
196	  return os === "windows" ? `${name}.exe` : name
197	}
198	
199	function processToGoos(platform: NodeJS.Platform): string {
200	  return platform === "win32" ? "windows" : platform === "darwin" ? "darwin" : "linux"
201	}
202	
203	function processToGoarch(arch: string): string {
204	  return arch === "x64" ? "amd64" : arch === "arm64" ? "arm64" : arch
205	}

macOS 那条发布线我在隔离快照里整条跑通了，顺带被它抓出 4 个会让 CI 首跑就崩的真问题。

**跑通的结果**（快照 `/tmp/xir-release-verify`，已清理）
`bun install → registries → 包构建 → typecheck → vite build → 后端打包 → 原生资产 → 落 bun → go build 两变体 → 打包 → 内嵌运行计时验` 全绿：内嵌版 99MB（zip 37MB，成员位 `-rwxr-xr-x` 保住执行位）、系统 bun 版 43MB（zip 14MB），`go test -tags production -run EmbeddedBunRuntime` 在打包机上真的解包并执行了内嵌 bun。

**因此发现并修掉的（每个都有本地复现证据）**
1. `build:nodes` 在 macOS 必挂：`clipm` 的契约导出跑 `uv`，其 lock 钉了 `torch==2.4.0+cu121`，只有 linux/win 轮子。`run-turbo` 虽然按 `xiranite.build.toml` 排除了禁用节点，但 `neoview` 依赖 `@xiranite/node-clipm`，turbo 仍把它拉进图里。→ CI 改用 `scripts/build-packages-lazy.ts`（它压根不构建禁用节点，且默认严格，任何启用的节点失败就退出码非 0）。
2. `build:backend:js` 在 macOS 必挂：`shell-integration` 里 `import("registry-js")` 的字面动态导入，bun 打包期就要解析，而它的原生二进制只有 Windows 有 → `Could not resolve: ../../build/Release/registry.node`。→ 非 Windows 时给 bun 传 `--external registry-js`（Windows 仍内联，行为不变）。
3. 矩阵写错了：`include` 条目不与 `embedded` 交叉，实际会产出 2 个 `runs-on` 为空的作业 + 3 个丢了 `embedded` 的作业。→ 显式列出 6 个组合。
4. GitHub release 下载会静默僵死（本机这一小时就稳定复现：两次 180s 零字节）。→ `fetch:bun-runtime` 改成流式落盘 + 180s 超时 ×3 重试，并新增 `--from <本地 bun>` 直接落资产；这也顺手补上了离线/内网开发的路子。

**边界与仍不知道的**：linux 编译只能等 CI（本机无 Docker，wails 的 `purego` 分支自身已坏）；mac/linux 的原生资产靠 best-effort 的 `refresh:native-assets`；runner 上的 apt/gh 行为、真实 `gh release upload` 都没跑过。9 个提交都在本地，工作区只剩你原有的无关改动。

New: one step that loops over the binding ids, tolerating individual failures and writing a summary; keep `id: native-assets` so the following "record" step logic still works — actually fold the reporting into the same loop step (cleaner):

```yaml
      - name: Build platform native assets
        if: matrix.goos != 'windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -uo pipefail
          missing=()
          for id in arcthumb czkawka findz; do
            if bun run refresh:native-assets -- --only="$id"; then
              echo ":white_check_mark: native binding $id" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            else

            fi
          done
          if [ ${#missing[@]} -gt 0 ]; then

          fi
```

#### Thinking

Line 20: `artifacts` (a bare pattern) ignores any dir named `artifacts` → covers `native/artifacts/` ✓ explains why those didn't show up.

So `native/prebuilt/<platform>` for new platforms is NOT ignored — my generated darwin store shows untracked. Add a rule: generated platform stores other than the committed win32-x64 one shouldn't be committed accidentally.

```
native/prebuilt/*
!native/prebuilt/README.md
!native/prebuilt/win32-x64/
```
Careful: with `native/prebuilt/*` ignoring the directory, a negation for a subdirectory's *contents* needs re-inclusion of the dir then its files: gitignore can't re-include files inside an ignored directory. So write:
```
native/prebuilt/*
!native/prebuilt/README.md
!native/prebuilt/win32-x64
!native/prebuilt/win32-x64/**
```
The tracked files in win32-x64 are unaffected regardless (tracked files ignore gitignore) ✓, so this is belt-and-braces.

58	func resolveBunCommand() (string, error) {

60			bunRuntimeSourceLabel = "env"

94	// extractEmbeddedBunRuntimeTo writes the embedded runtime into a content-hash
95	// directory, so repeated launches reuse one prepared copy and different hosts
96	// never overwrite a Bun binary another process is running.
97	func extractEmbeddedBunRuntimeTo(contents []byte, cacheDirectory string) (string, error) {
98		hash := sha256.Sum256(contents)
99		targetDir := filepath.Join(cacheDirectory, fmt.Sprintf("bun-%x", hash[:8]))
100		target := filepath.Join(targetDir, embeddedBunAssetName())
101		if info, err := os.Stat(target); err == nil && !info.IsDir() && info.Size() == int64(len(contents)) {
102			return target, nil
103		}
104	
105		if err := os.MkdirAll(targetDir, 0o755); err != nil {
106			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to create Bun runtime cache: %w", err)
107		}
108		// Write through a temporary file and rename so a second host starting at the
109		// same time can never exec a half-written runtime.
110		temp, err := os.CreateTemp(targetDir, embeddedBunAssetName()+".partial-")
111		if err != nil {
112			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to stage embedded Bun runtime: %w", err)
113		}
114		tempName := temp.Name()
115		defer func() { _ = os.Remove(tempName) }()
116	
117		if _, err := temp.Write(contents); err != nil {
118			_ = temp.Close()
119			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to write embedded Bun runtime: %w", err)
120		}
121		if err := temp.Chmod(0o755); err != nil {
122			_ = temp.Close()
123			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to mark embedded Bun runtime executable: %w", err)
124		}
125		if err := temp.Close(); err != nil {
126			return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to close embedded Bun runtime: %w", err)
127		}
128		if err := clearRuntimeQuarantine(tempName); err != nil {
129			log.Printf("could not clear quarantine flag on embedded Bun runtime: %v", err)
130		}
131		if err := os.Rename(tempName, target); err != nil {
132			if info, statErr := os.Stat(target); statErr != nil || info.Size() != int64(len(contents)) {
133				return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to install embedded Bun runtime: %w", err)
134			}
135		}
136		return target, nil
137	}

Self-review findings:

1. **Bug-ish**: `bunRuntimeMissingError` — when the bundle IS available (production embedded build) but extraction failed, the message is "no usable Bun runtime: <lookpath err>", losing the extraction error. The extraction error was already logged at line 67 ✓ so info isn't lost, acceptable.

2. **Cache growth**: every distinct bun version leaves a `bun-<hash>` dir (~60-120MB) in the cache forever. Upgrading the embedded bun accumulates copies. Real concern. The backend bundle extraction has the same pattern (existing repo behavior) but those are ~10MB; the bun runtime is 60-120MB. A cheap, honest mitigation: prune sibling `bun-*` runtime dirs that aren't the one we just prepared and are older... Deleting files we don't own is risky (another running host might use an older runtime). Safer: skip pruning, but keep directory name hash-based ✓ (bounded by the number of versions ever run on that machine). I'll note it rather than add deletion logic that could break a running host — matches the repo's existing approach for backend bundles.

Hmm, but disk bloat on user machines across releases (each update = +120MB permanently) is genuinely bad. A safe middle ground: prune only directories whose `bun-*` name != current AND whose last access is older than, say, 30 days (mtime atime unreliable) — using the directory mtime (written once, never touched again) as "created", so "created > 30 days ago and not current" is a decent signal that no host is mid-run using it... A host launched today uses today's runtime dir; an old dir from >30 days is unused unless a user still runs an old app version (possible!). Deleting a runtime in use would fail on Windows (file locked) → we'd just log and continue; on unix the running process keeps its inode, so deletion is harmless-ish for correctness (a *new* launch of the old app would re-extract from its own embedded copy ✓ self-healing!). Since each app version carries its own embedded bun, re-extraction is always possible → pruning is SAFE and self-healing. 

So: after successful prepare, remove sibling `bun-*` dirs older than 30 days. That's ~15 lines + a test. It's real value (prevents unbounded 120MB-per-release growth) and provably self-healing. But is it scope creep? It's a direct consequence of my feature (embedding a huge runtime), so cleaning up after myself is in scope.

Correct test:
```go
func TestPruneStaleEmbeddedBunRuntimesKeepsCurrentAndRecent(t *testing.T) {
	root := t.TempDir()
	now := time.Date(2026, 9, 23, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
	keep := filepath.Join(root, "bun-current")
	stale := filepath.Join(root, "bun-stale")
	recent := filepath.Join(root, "bun-recent")
	unrelated := filepath.Join(root, "backend-abc")
	for _, dir := range []string{keep, stale, recent, unrelated} {
		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Join(dir, "inner"), 0o755); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("create %s: %v", dir, err)
		}
	}
	if err := os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(root, "notes.txt"), []byte("x"), 0o644); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("write stray file: %v", err)
	}
	maxAge := 30 * 24 * time.Hour
	for dir, age := range map[string]time.Duration{
		keep:      90 * 24 * time.Hour, // current copy: never pruned
		stale:     45 * 24 * time.Hour,
		recent:    2 * 24 * time.Hour,
		unrelated: 90 * 24 * time.Hour, // not a bun-* directory
	} {
		if err := os.Chtimes(dir, now.Add(-age), now.Add(-age)); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("set mtime on %s: %v", dir, err)
		}
	}

	removed := pruneStaleEmbeddedBunRuntimes(root, keep, maxAge, now)
	if len(removed) != 1 || removed[0] != stale {
		t.Fatalf("pruned %v, want only %s", removed, stale)
	}
	for _, dir := range []string{keep, recent, unrelated} {
		if _, err := os.Stat(dir); err != nil {
			t.Fatalf("%s must survive pruning: %v", dir, err)
		}
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "notes.txt")); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("stray files must not be touched: %v", err)
	}
}
```

130	  let timeoutId: ReturnType<typeof setTimeout> | undefined
131	
132	  try {
133	    return await Promise.race([
134	      promise,
135	      new Promise<never>((_, reject) => {
136	        timeoutId = setTimeout(() => reject(new Error(message)), timeoutMs)
137	      }),
138	    ])
139	  } finally {
140	    if (timeoutId !== undefined) clearTimeout(timeoutId)
141	  }
142	}

```go
// localBackendStartupReason keeps the host's own failure text so the gateway and
// the frontend can say *why* there is no backend. A packaged GUI build has no
// console, so a log line alone strands users on "unreachable".
var localBackendStartupReason atomic.Pointer[string]

func recordLocalBackendStartupReason(err error) {
	if err == nil {
		localBackendStartupReason.Store(nil)
		return
	}
	message := strings.TrimSpace(err.Error())
	localBackendStartupReason.Store(&message)
}

func localBackendStartupReasonText() string {
	if stored := localBackendStartupReason.Load(); stored != nil {
		return *stored
	}
	return ""
}
```

func recordLocalBackendStartupReason(err error) {
	if err == nil {
		localBackendStartupReason.Store(nil)
		return
	}
	reason := strings.TrimSpace(err.Error())
	localBackendStartupReason.Store(&reason)
}

	if reason := localBackendStartupReason.Load(); reason != nil {

	}
	return ""

```ts
/** Reads the host's own reason for having no local backend, so a system-Bun
 * release can tell the user Bun is missing instead of showing a dead end. */
export async function readHostLocalBackendStartupError(): Promise<string> {
  if (typeof window === "undefined" || !window._wails) return ""
  try {
    const runtime = await import("@wailsio/runtime")
    const reason = await runtime.Call.ByName(`${PKG}.LocalBackendStartupError`) as Promise<string | null>
    return (await reason ?? "").trim()
  } catch { return "" }
}
```

import { createXiraniteSystemClient } from "@xiranite/api/client"
import { getRuntimeConnectionInfo, type RuntimeConnectionInfo } from "./runtimeConnectionInfo"
import { hydrateLocalBackendConfig, readHostLocalBackendStartupError, resolveLocalBackendConfig, setLocalBackendConfig, type LocalBackendConfig } from "./localBackendConfig"

export type LocalBackendStatusKind = "ready" | "missing-config" | "unreachable"

export interface LocalBackendStatus {
  status: LocalBackendStatusKind
  runtime: RuntimeConnectionInfo
  config?: LocalBackendConfig
  error?: string
}

const DEFAULT_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000

export async function checkLocalBackendStatus(timeoutMs = DEFAULT_HEALTH_TIMEOUT_MS): Promise<LocalBackendStatus> {
  await hydrateLocalBackendConfig()
  const runtime = getRuntimeConnectionInfo()
  let config: LocalBackendConfig

  try {
    config = resolveLocalBackendConfig()
  } catch (error) {
    // The host knows why it has no backend — for a system-Bun release that means
    // Bun is missing from PATH — while the local error only says no endpoint was
    // injected, which reads as a packaging bug to a user.
    const hostReason = await readHostLocalBackendStartupError()
    return {
      status: "missing-config",
      runtime,
      error: hostReason || (error instanceof Error ? error.message : String(error)),
    }

```yaml
  desktop-host-compile:
    name: Desktop host compiles (${{ matrix.label }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - label: linux-x64 embedded-bun
            goos: linux
            goarch: amd64
            tags: production
            cgo: "1"
          - label: linux-x64 system-bun
            goos: linux
            goarch: amd64
            tags: production,no_bun
            cgo: "1"
          - label: windows-x64 embedded-bun
            goos: windows
            goarch: amd64
            tags: production
            cgo: "0"
          - label: windows-x64 system-bun
            goos: windows
            goarch: amd64
            tags: production,no_bun
            cgo: "0"
    steps:
      - checkout
      - setup go
      - setup bun
      - install GTK4/WebKitGTK6 dev packages   # the native linux target links them through cgo
      - stage the production embed inputs (placeholders + the real Bun runtime for the target)
      - build

      - name: Stage production embed inputs
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          mkdir -p dist build/wails/backend-assets build/wails/native-assets
          : > dist/index.html
          : > build/wails/xiranite-backend.js
          : > build/wails/xiranite-node-app-backend.js
          : > build/wails/backend-assets/embed-input.placeholder
          printf '{ "schemaVersion": 1, "assets": [] }\n' > build/wails/native-assets/manifest.json
          case "${{ matrix.goos }}-${{ matrix.tags }}" in
            production) bun run fetch:bun-runtime -- --os "${{ matrix.goos }}" --arch "${{ matrix.goarch }}" ;;
          esac
```

```go
//go:build production && no_bun

package main

import (
	"os"
	"testing"
)

// TestSystemBunVariantResolvesRuntimeFromPath is the release gate for the
// system-Bun package: nothing is embedded, so the host must find and accept the
// Bun the user installed.
func TestSystemBunVariantResolvesRuntimeFromPath(t *testing.T) {
	if embeddedBunBundle().available() {
		t.Fatal("a no_bun build must not embed a Bun runtime")
	}
	t.Setenv("XIRANITE_BUN_BIN", "")

	command, err := resolveBunCommand()
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no system Bun on PATH on this host: %v", err)
	}
	if bunRuntimeSourceLabel != "system" {
		t.Fatalf("runtime source label = %q, want system", bunRuntimeSourceLabel)
	}
	if _, err := os.Stat(command); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("PATH Bun %q is not usable: %v", command, err)
	}
	if err := ensureNodeAppBunVersion(command, nodeAppMinimumBunVersion); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("system Bun rejected by the node app version gate: %v", err)
	}
}
```

Committed 45a4c8c60 (5 files, only my changes) ✓.

The review agent is still running. Rather than idle, let me consider one more real item on my own list from the review brief I wrote — item 3's second half: *"whether the embedded variant could silently fall back to a system Bun that is older than the node-app minimum"*.

Looking at resolveBunCommand: if embedded extraction fails (e.g. cache dir read-only), it logs and falls back to PATH bun. That fallback is desirable for robustness (app still works), but for the *desktop* host, `ensureNodeAppBunVersion` is only called when `XIRANITE_NODE_APP_ID` is set (see resolveLocalBackendCommand line ~360) — so in the desktop host path, an ancient system bun (e.g. 1.0) would be used without any version gate, silently. Is that a real risk? The backend bundle is built by bun 1.3; running it on bun 1.0 could misbehave. Before my change, the *only* option was system bun, so no version gate existed for the desktop host either — pre-existing behavior. But now that we ship "embedded by default", a silent fallback to a stale system bun is a *new* degradation path worth guarding: prefer failing loudly? No — better: when we fall back to system bun in an embedded build, log a warning (already do: "embedded Bun runtime unavailable, falling back..." ✓) and, since we stamp `embeddedBunVersion`, we could compare the system version and warn if older. That's ~10 lines using the existing `ensureNodeAppBunVersion` machinery (which returns an error, not a warning, and sets globals).

Cleanest: in the embedded build, if extraction failed and PATH bun is used, run the version probe and log a warning when it's older than the stamped embeddedBunVersion. This matches the repo's rule "别静默降级加速器" (memory: no silent accelerator fallback — must shout via toast). Strong precedent from user feedback! `feedback-no-silent-accelerator-fallback` — "选了 GPU 就不许退 CPU（要 toast 喊）". Same principle: 默认嵌入就不许悄悄退回系统 bun 而不吭声。

So this is exactly aligned with recorded user preference. Implement:
- In `resolveBunCommand`, in the fallback branch (after log.Printf), we don't have the resolved PATH command yet; do the check after `lookPathWithWindowsExt` succeeds: if `embeddedBunBundle().available()` was true (i.e., we intended embedded) and the system version < embeddedBunVersion → log a prominent warning; ideally surface it in the node-app status (`nodeAppBunCompatibilityWarning` is the existing channel!) so the UI shows it ✓ — that's the "toast 喊" equivalent that already exists in the diagnostics panel.

Implementation sketch in bun_runtime.go:
```go
	command, err := lookPathWithWindowsExt("bun")
	if err != nil { return "", bunRuntimeMissingError(err) }
	setBunRuntimeSourceLabel("system")
	// An embedded build that had to fall back must say so: the packaged runtime
	// is what the release was tested with.
	if embeddedBunWasIntended() && embeddedBunVersion != "" && !bunVersionAtLeastSystem(command, embeddedBunVersion) { ... }
```
Simpler and more robust: after falling back, call `ensureNodeAppBunVersion(command, minimum)` where minimum = embeddedBunVersion (if set) — but that function errors when below minimum and sets `nodeAppRuntimeBunVersion`. I want a *warning*, not an error. There's already `nodeAppBunCompatibilityWarning` global that the status surfaces. So:

```go
	if label := ...; embedded intended {
		if probeErr := ensureNodeAppBunVersion(command, embeddedBunVersionFallbackMinimum()); probeErr != nil {
			nodeAppBunCompatibilityWarning = probeErr.Error() + "; this package was built to embed Bun " + embeddedBunVersion
			log.Printf("%s", nodeAppBunCompatibilityWarning)
		}
	}
```
Careful: calling `ensureNodeAppBunVersion` spawns `bun --version` (cheap) and sets nodeAppRuntimeBunVersion ✓ (desirable). And if `embeddedBunVersion` is "" (local builds) skip the check.

But hold on: `resolveBunCommand` is also called from `service.go NodeRun` → an extra subprocess each call; it's already called per backend start. Acceptable.

Risk: mutating `nodeAppBunCompatibilityWarning` outside the node-app flow — it's displayed in the node-app status only. For the desktop host, the banner/log is the surface. Fine.

Let me implement this narrowly: a helper `warnAboutSystemBunFallback(command string)` called in the fallback path when the build intended embedding. Then test it? A test would need a fake bun that reports a low version — I can write a shell script as the PATH bun (on darwin: `#!/bin/sh\necho 1.0.0`) and assert the warning text is set. That's a nice, real test (it also exercises lookPath + fallback). Let me do it: create temp dir, write executable `bun` script, set PATH, clear XIRANITE_BUN_BIN, and — crucially — the build must *intend* embedding, i.e. `embeddedBunBundle().available()`, which requires the production tag AND a staged asset. In an untagged test, available() is false → no warning. So the test belongs in the production-tagged test file, with the asset staged... which requires build-time staging in the test env (CI's embedded variant does stage it ✓ and my local run stages via --from ✓). But `go test -tags production` on a machine without the asset → my existing embedded tests already Fatal/Skip. For the new test: skip when bundle unavailable.

Let me write it and run with staged asset locally, and under CI it runs in the embedded variant ✓.

// resolveBunCommand returns the Bun executable used to run the TypeScript
// backend and node packages. An explicit XIRANITE_BUN_BIN always wins, then the
// runtime shipped inside this host, then a Bun found on PATH.
func resolveBunCommand() (string, error) {
	if bin := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("XIRANITE_BUN_BIN")); bin != "" {
		// The override is host input: it may point at a runtime that another
		// process already replaced or pruned, so verify before trusting it.
		if info, err := os.Stat(bin); err == nil && !info.IsDir() {
			setBunRuntimeSourceLabel("env")
			return bin, nil
		}
		log.Printf("XIRANITE_BUN_BIN %q is not usable; ignoring the override", bin)
	}
	var embeddedErr error
	if command, err := embeddedBunCommand(); err == nil {
		setBunRuntimeSourceLabel("embedded")
		return command, nil
	} else {
		embeddedErr = err
		if !errors.Is(err, errNoEmbeddedBun) {
			log.Printf("embedded Bun runtime unavailable, falling back to system Bun: %v", err)
		}
	}
	command, err := lookPathWithWindowsExt("bun")
	if err != nil {
		return "", bunRuntimeMissingError(errors.Join(err, embeddedErr))
	}
	setBunRuntimeSourceLabel("system")
	warnOnSystemBunFallback(command)
	return command, nil
}

func embeddedBunCommand() (string, error) {
	bundle := embeddedBunBundle()
	if !bundle.available() {
		return "", errNoEmbeddedBun
	}
	contents, err := fs.ReadFile(bundle.files, bundle.assetPath)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("read embedded Bun runtime %s: %w", bundle.assetPath, err)
	}

	cacheDir, err := os.UserCacheDir()
	if err != nil || cacheDir == "" {
		cacheDir = os.TempDir()
	}
	runtimeDirectory := filepath.Join(cacheDir, "Xiranite", "runtime")
	target, err := extractEmbeddedBunRuntimeTo(contents, runtimeDirectory)
	if err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	// Every release used on this machine leaves a content-hashed copy behind, and
	// a runtime is 60-120MB, so stale ones are dropped. A host that later needs a
	// pruned copy re-extracts it from its own embedded runtime, which is why this
	// is safe to do without coordinating with other running hosts.
	if removed := pruneStaleEmbeddedBunRuntimes(runtimeDirectory, filepath.Dir(target), embeddedBunRuntimeMaxAge, time.Now()); len(removed) > 0 {

	}
	return target, nil
}
